title: Full-Text Search Ranking and Highlighting
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose and main terms of Full-Text Search Ranking and Highlighting.
Use or interpret an appropriate PostgreSQL example connected to search ranking.
Identify one edge case and select a safe way to verify the expected result.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on Full-Text Search Ranking and Highlighting. Its primary job is to help you query document-shaped JSON and searchable text while choosing when relational columns or extensions are better. The listed PDF subtopics define the coverage expected here; work through them in order and connect each one to an example, edge case and checkable result.
content.why_it_matters: This topic matters because PostgreSQL systems must preserve correct results as data grows and more sessions or services interact with it. Practicing full-text search ranking and highlighting teaches you to make assumptions explicit, apply the right SQL or operational tool, and verify behavior instead of relying on a demonstration that only worked once.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Keep the problem small: query document-shaped JSON and searchable text while choosing when relational columns or extensions are better. A PostgreSQL feature should be chosen for the semantics it provides, not just because it is available. Before executing a change, state the inputs, expected output and boundary conditions. The example below is intentionally small enough to inspect; it illustrates the idea but is not a substitute for a test against your schema and PostgreSQL version.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Full-Text Search Ranking and Highlighting
content_blocks.code:
SELECT to_tsvector('english', 'PostgreSQL makes database search useful')
       @@ plainto_tsquery('english', 'database search') AS matches;
content_blocks.expected_output:
matches
-------
t

The exact lexemes depend on the selected text-search configuration.
content_blocks.safety_note: Check language configuration and ranking behavior against representative text.

content_blocks.title: Practical checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Version note: PostgreSQL 18.6 is the primary reference. PostgreSQL 19 beta/development features are not assumed to be stable.

task: Create a short practice artifact for “Full-Text Search Ranking and Highlighting”: explain its goal, show one example linked to “Search ranking”, state the expected result, and include one edge/failure case and verification method. Use a disposable database or static artifact as appropriate.
hints: Start with the listed subtopics, especially “Search ranking”, and describe the expected behavior in your own words.
Run or inspect the smallest example that demonstrates the behavior; do not add unrelated features before it is verified.
When the result surprises you, capture the exact SQL/error, check version and permissions, and change one assumption at a time.
expected_output: A reviewable note or query for Full-Text Search Ranking and Highlighting, with an explanation of “Search ranking”, expected behavior, and a documented edge-case check.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying the example without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Object names, data types, privileges, extensions and data distribution affect database behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: List schema/version assumptions and test with a tiny synthetic dataset first.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating a single successful query as proof of production readiness.
common_mistakes.why: A happy-path result does not test invalid input, concurrent sessions, permissions, recovery or query performance.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one negative/edge case and record the evidence that confirms the expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: Making a production change directly from a lesson.
common_mistakes.why: DDL, data updates, role changes and operational commands can affect data or availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use an isolated lab, reviewed migration, least privilege, rollback/recovery plan and a second-person review for production.

summary: Full-Text Search Ranking and Highlighting fits into the broader goal to query document-shaped JSON and searchable text while choosing when relational columns or extensions are better.
Use the curriculum subtopics as a completeness checklist: Search ranking, Relevance ordering, Highlighting matches.
State the schema/version assumptions and verify one normal case plus an edge case before trusting the result.
